messages:
Anya: Heads-up, us-west GPU pool saturated starting ~13:05 UTC, requests piled into the admission queue and we saw downstream fallthrough to CPU pods causing tail-latency spikes.
incident-bot: Incident INC-472 created by Anya: region us-west gpu-starvation -> cascading downstream overload.
Matt: Noted. Which stack did customers hit first? frontend or batch?
Anya: Mostly real-time generation (api-route /v1/generate) — the router started admitting more than available slots because slot accounting drifted after yesterday's deploy.
Jen SRE: I'm seeing continuous backpressure in the runtime queue stats. admission_controller.allowed_rate jumped even though available_gpus = 0. Possibly token-bucket reset bug.
Kyle: Autoscaler didn't add more GPU nodes; quota checks returned 403 from cloud provider. We were at soft quota and autoscaler refused to request increase.
Samir: Also saw cross-region replica lag spike — requests that fell back to us-east hit network egress limits and retried, amplifying load.
Ron Infra: I pulled the kube-proxy and node metrics. Node GPU memory is fine, pods are pending due to no allocatable GPU resources.
Anya: Immediate mitigation: reduced ingress rate by 50% via circuit-breaker on API gateway and toggled conservative admission policy (deny-when-uncertain). Deploying now.
deploy-bot: Rollout started: ingress-circuitbreaker v2 -> canary 10% -> target 50%
Jen SRE: Canary looks good so far, queue depth halved. Looking at runtime logs:
```
runtime.admission: allow=true reason="slot_mismatch" slots_requested=1 slots_available=0
queue.length=482 -> 218 after gate
```
Jen SRE: The allow=true despite slots_available=0 is the root symptom. Need to trace admission-controller state replication.
Matt: Who owns the admission-controller change from yesterday? IIRC Kyle merged it.
Kyle: That was me. I pushed a change to prefer latency over strict slot checks to reduce 429s during transient GC. But I didn't account for region-wide quota exhaustion. Rolling a revert to re-enable strict slot validation.
Samir: Cost note: during the fallback to CPU we consumed ~3x more tokens worth of compute (longer runs per request), cost spike ~+18% in us-west for the hour.
Anya: Agreed, we'll include a cost action item. After rollback and ingress throttle, error rates are trending down. Planning: postmortem, revert fix, add preflight quota check, and an autoscaler policy to request quota increases.
Jen SRE: Action items: 1) revert admission change (Kyle) 2) add preflight quota+region check (Ron/Kyle) 3) circuit-breaker default for region on overload (Matt) 4) run a chaos test for slot accounting (Samir). Assigning owners in follow-up doc.
Anya: Thanks — will file the postmortem and assign JIRA tasks. Closing temporary incident channel when all mitigations verified. :white_check_mark:
